sections.h2: What should I expect when selling a house in Linden, NJ?
sections.html:
Linden is a dense industrial and residential city in Union County, about 13 miles southwest of Manhattan, and sellers here deal with a mix of two-family houses, rentals and older single-family homes. You can list the house, sell it without an agent, or accept a cash purchase as-is. The deed then goes to the Union County Clerk in Elizabeth, and the seller pays the state's transfer fee.

The Census Bureau estimates 45,752 residents for July 1, 2025, up 4.6% from the April 2020 base. The city has 10.69 square miles of land, and Linden also holds a slice of water frontage along the Arthur Kill, which separates it from Staten Island.

sections.h2: How did Linden develop, and where are its neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Linden was formed as a township on March 4, 1861, from pieces of Elizabeth, Rahway and Union Township. Cranford, Linden Borough and Roselle were later carved from it. The borough and township were merged and incorporated as a city on January 1, 1925, and the name comes from linden trees brought from Germany.

The population shows how late the growth came: 8,368 people in 1920, 21,206 in 1930, and 39,931 by 1960. Named areas inside the city include Bayway, Grasselli, Tremley, Wheatsheaf, Morses Mill, Vreeland Mills and Warners. The residential section west of St. Georges Avenue is called Sunnyside, named for a former golf club. Linden borders Clark, Cranford, Elizabeth, Rahway, Roselle and Winfield Township in Union County, plus Carteret and Woodbridge across the county line.

Linden is also a regional center of Polish settlement. About 13.1% of residents report Polish origin, and the city holds an annual Polish Heritage Day Festival.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Linden homes?
sections.html:
A little under 60% of Linden homes are lived in by their owners, and about 36% of residents were born outside the United States. The median owner-occupied home was valued at $419,700 for 2020 to 2024.

With 56.7% of residents speaking a language other than English at home, translated listing materials and a closing attorney who can explain documents in the seller's language can help.

sections.h2: What industry and employers shape Linden's housing market?
sections.html:
The east side of Linden follows the Arthur Kill, a shipping channel in the Port of New York and New Jersey. The Bayway Refinery, operated by Phillips 66, refines about 230,000 barrels a day and is the second-largest on the East Coast. Census data for 2022 show roughly $517 million in transportation and warehousing receipts and $1.53 billion in retail sales in the city.

General Motors ran Linden Assembly from 1937 to 2005, and most of the plant was later torn down for a redevelopment on a 100-acre site. Merck, one of the larger pharmaceutical companies in the country, is based across Linden and Rahway.

Commuting is a selling point for many Linden houses. The Census records a mean commute of 31.5 minutes, and the options are broad:

  • Rail: Linden station offers a one-seat ride to Manhattan in 39 minutes on the North Jersey Coast Line and Northeast Corridor Line.
  • Highways: the New Jersey Turnpike runs through the east side, Interstate 278 ends in Linden, and U.S. 1/9 and Route 27 cross the city. The Garden State Parkway passes about 500 feet west of the city limits.
  • Bus: NJ Transit routes 112 and 115 reach the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and routes 48 and 94 go to Elizabeth and Newark.
  • Air: Newark Liberty International Airport is about 15 minutes away, and Linden Airport handles small general aviation flights.

If your house is within walking distance of the station, say so in the first line of the listing or offer request.

sections.h2: What are the public schools in Linden?
sections.html: Linden Public Schools serve prekindergarten through grade 12 with 11 schools and 6,125 students in 2022-23. Eight elementary schools (Schools 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10) cover PreK to grade 5, McManus Middle School and Soehl Middle School cover grades 6 to 8, and Linden High School had 1,801 students. School No. 5 was named a National Blue Ribbon School in 2020. A buyer with children will ask which numbered school serves a given block, so have the answer ready.

sections.h2: What local steps does a Linden seller handle before closing?
sections.html:
Contact the City of Linden's construction and code office to ask whether a continued certificate of occupancy, fire inspection or smoke and carbon monoxide certificate must be on file before the deed is delivered. Ask also about open permits on the property and any fines attached to the tax account. Get the answers in writing so the buyer's attorney can see them.

The Union County Clerk's recording office is at 2 Broad Street in Elizabeth, phone 908-527-4787. It is open Monday to Friday from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, with over-the-counter recording from 8:30 AM to 3:30 PM and no appointment required. The clerk's online land records run from June 1, 1977 forward, and the office offers a free property fraud alert program that notifies a subscriber when their name appears on a recording.

For the transfer fee, Linden's median value of $419,700 puts a typical sale in the schedule for prices over $350,000. That schedule charges $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000, $4.25 per $500 up to $200,000 and $4.80 per $500 up to $550,000. The state also charges a percentage fee on residential deeds above $1 million, and the seller is responsible for both.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a good fit for a Linden house?
sections.html:
It can be, if the house needs work, has tenants, or you need a firm closing date. A cash buyer purchasing as-is removes repair requests and mortgage approval from the timeline. A listing may still produce a higher price on a house in good condition, since it reaches owner-occupants and investors alike.

Ask each buyer for written terms and compare them line by line: price, closing date, who pays the transfer fee, and who handles any city inspection. Two offers with the same headline number can leave you with different amounts at the table. Linden's mix of one-family houses, two-family houses and rentals means the right buyer type varies block by block, so ask your agent or closing attorney who has bought on your street recently. Ask the Union County Clerk's office or your title company for a copy of your last recorded deed, and keep the survey, tax bills and any permit paperwork together in one folder.

faqs.q: Does Linden require an inspection before a home sale?
faqs.a: Ask the City of Linden's construction and code office. Resale inspection rules differ from one New Jersey municipality to the next, so confirm in writing whether a certificate is needed for your address and how long scheduling takes.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee on a Linden sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. The fee is calculated on the deed price and paid when the deed is recorded with the Union County Clerk. Sales over $1 million add a graduated percent fee, also paid by the seller.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Linden house?
faqs.a: At the Union County Clerk's recording office, 2 Broad Street, Elizabeth. It takes recordings Monday to Friday and does not require an appointment for recording.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Linden two-family house or rental with tenants in place?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer the leases and rent roll, and check with the city whether a rental registration or inspection is attached to the property. Ask each buyer in writing whether they will purchase with tenants in place.

faqs.q: How fast can a Linden house sale close?
faqs.a: Timing depends on the buyer type and the city paperwork. A cash purchase has no mortgage underwriting, so it can close sooner, but the deed recording and any required city certificate still take their own time.
